Redox-differentiated bank filtration is associated with enhanced sulfamethoxazole transformation but sustains persistent transformation products
Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
articles.abstract: Abstract Land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) is altering greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics in coastal wetlands, yet how these responses vary among ecosystems and conversion pathways remains uncertain. Here, we synthesized 276 studies and applied multilevel meta-analysis to paired LULCC comparisons. GHG responses varied with pre-conversion wetland type, destination land use, hydrology, and soil carbon and nitrogen status. Pooled sustained-flux global warming potential (SGWP) was ‒122.41 ± 81.99 mg CO 2 e m ‒2 h ‒1 for natural coastal wetlands and 250.60 ± 101.06 for LULCC sites, corresponding to 0.17 ± 0.06 Gt CO 2 e of cumulative emissions over two decades. The descriptive SGWP contrast with pooled LULCC sites was larger for vegetated wetlands ( + 309.32%) than for tidal flats ( + 165.02%). Ecologically restored wetlands showed negative pooled SGWP ( − 33.03 ± 114.70 mg CO 2 e m ‒2 h ‒1 ), contrasting with the positive pooled LULCC estimate. Our results indicate that GHG responses to coastal wetland conversion are ecosystem- and pathway-specific, underscoring the importance of conserving vegetated wetlands and targeting restoration.

articles.title: A highly distorted benzenium cation
articles.abstract: Abstract In contrast to the well-explored peripheral functionalization of benzene, its skeletal alteration remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a highly distorted benzenium cation, 2,3-dihydroxy-1,4,6-triamino-5-nitrobenzenium (TANBC + ), featuring a ring twist angle of 35.91° and a ring C-C bond length of 1.540 Å, both rank the highest among all benzenium cations. Such pronounced structural distortions endow TANBC + with unique electronic properties, including a highly positive electrostatic charge on the warped carbon, weak aromaticity, and a low ring bond dissociation energy. Consequently, instead of undergoing peripheral functionalization like typical benzenium cations, TANBC + participates in three distinct benzene ring reconstruction pathways or remains inert under standard electrophilic substitution conditions. Moreover, despite its distorted structure, TANBC + exhibits excellent ambient stability, stabilized by extensive hydrogen bonding, and can be synthesized readily without harsh conditions usually required for conventional benzenium cations. This work not only introduces a new strategy for benzene reconstruction but also redefines the role of benzenium cations from mediators of peripheral functionalization to promoters of skeletal alteration, thereby advancing the fundamental chemistry of benzene.

articles.title: Shape conforming Janus hydrogel for preventing anastomotic leaks
Structural basis for constitutive activation of oncogenic gp130 mutants found in human inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas
Visible light drives bright extreme-ultraviolet high harmonics
articles.abstract: Abstract Coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) light is a central tool in modern photon science, probing the electronic, chemical and structural properties of matter. High-harmonic generation can extend the reach of laser sources into this spectral range, but the achievable photon flux falls sharply as photon energy increases. We show experimentally and theoretically that plasma-core-induced self-guiding of a visible-wavelength driver in helium sustains high intensity and favorable phase matching over an extended propagation length. We achieve a conversion efficiency of up to 10 −6 in a single high-harmonic line and phase-matched emission extending to 100 eV. With less than 10 W of average power at 516 nm from a frequency-doubled ytterbium laser, we generate 1.8 × 10 11 photons s −1 within 2 % bandwidth at 13.5 nm (91.8 eV), exceeding previous reports by more than an order of magnitude. These results establish a power-scalable XUV platform for actinic metrology, spectroscopy and coherent imaging.

articles.title: [c2]Daisy-chain molecular turing machines with switchable fluorescence outputs
G3BP1-induced retrograde transport blockade triggers HSC activation and liver fibrosis via COPI alternative splicing
Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
articles.abstract: Abstract The adsorption energy serves as a crucial descriptor for the large-scale screening of catalysts. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of training data for the extensively utilised machine learning interatomic potential, predominantly sourced from near-equilibrium structures, results in unreliable adsorption structures and consequent adsorption energy predictions. In this context, we present DBCata, a deep generative model that integrates a periodic Brownian-bridge framework with an equivariant graph neural network to establish a low-dimensional transition manifold between unrelaxed and DFT-relaxed structures, without requiring explicit energy or force information. Upon training, DBCata effectively generates high-fidelity adsorption geometries, achieving an interatomic distance mean absolute error of 0.035 Å on the dataset from Catalysis-Hub, which is approximately 70% lower than that of the current state-of-the-art machine learning potential models. Moreover, the corresponding DFT accuracy can be improved within 0.1 eV in 94% of instances by identifying and refining anomalous predictions through a hybrid chemical-heuristic and self-supervised outlier detection approach. We demonstrate that DBCata enables accelerated high-throughput computational screening for alloy catalysts in the oxygen reduction reaction, highlighting the potential of DBCata as a powerful tool for catalyst design and optimisation.

articles.title: Entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity enables near-decoupled polarization–strain behavior for high-density energy storage
Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids
articles.abstract: Abstract Tabernanthe iboga (iboga) is the source of voacangine, which is widely used as a semi-synthetic starting material for the anti-addiction agent ibogaine. Despite extensive investigation of voacangine biosynthesis, production of this compound cannot be reconstituted in a heterologous host, suggesting that one or more enzymes required for biosynthesis are missing. Additionally, T. iboga produces ibophyllidine, a pyrroloindole alkaloid that utilizes the same upstream precursor as voacangine, but is a member of a structurally distinct alkaloid class. Here we use bulk and single cell gene expression from leaf and root tissue to identify the unknown enzymes from these two pathways. We identify two additional enzymes that enable biosynthesis of voacangine in a heterologous host. The missing enzymes includes a pathogenesis-related (PR)10 family protein that likely catalyzes cyclization of a transient intermediate. Careful analysis of gene expression profiles in leaf and root also enabled the discovery of four additional enzymes that convert an upstream intermediate to ibophyllidine. This work reveals the chemical logic that generates two distinct alkaloid scaffolds in this important medicinal plant.

articles.title: Landscape fire sourced PM2.5, cause-specific paediatric hospitalisations, and the role of tree cover
Plankton ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven weakening of the ocean biological pump
Influenza A virus orchestrates ciliated cell fate and injury during the mucociliary damage repair cycle
articles.abstract: Abstract Influenza A virus causes acute damage to airway epithelium, yet the damage–repair cycle and mechanisms underlying persistent mucociliary clearance (MCC) dysfunction long after viral clearance remain unclear. Here, using longitudinal in vivo quantitative micro-optical coherence tomography, we show that global MCC impairment persists for more than 14 days, marked by impaired ciliary activity and sustained mucus hypersecretion in male mice infected with the H1N1 influenza A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8) strain. Through lineage tracing and multi-omics analyses, we identify an immune-mediated transdifferentiation program in which IFN signaling activates the IDO1–AhR axis to drive ciliated-to-mucous cell fate transition and chronic muco-obstruction after H1N1 PR8 infection in a reconstructed human bronchial epithelium model. In parallel, we identify the viral M2 protein as a key driver of ciliary loss, suppressing the host TP73–FOXJ1–RFX3 regulatory axis and promoting proteasomal degradation of FOXJ1. Together, these findings uncover host- and virus-driven pathways that cooperatively impair airway epithelial homeostasis and sustain MCC failure beyond active infection, highlighting therapeutic targets for post-influenza muco-obstructive disease.

articles.title: A global atlas of digital dermatology to map innovation and disparities
articles.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence promises democratized access to dermatological care, but model reliability depends on the quality and comprehensiveness of the underlying data. Despite rapid growth in publicly available dermatology images, the field lacks quantitative indicators to measure whether new datasets expand clinical coverage or merely replicate what is already known. Existing collections are widely assumed to be biased, yet the scale and topography of these gaps have remained unquantified, leaving the community without a road map for strategic data acquisition. Here, we show, by unifying 1.1 million images from 29 public datasets into a queryable semantic atlas, that the global archive is markedly skewed and increasingly redundant: darker skin tones (Fitzpatrick V–VI) constitute only 11.0% of images, pediatric patients only 2.3%, and informational novelty has plateaued despite exponential growth, revealing where targeted data acquisition is most needed.

articles.title: Localized strain-engineered 1D electron guides in 2D MoS2 devices with synaptic memory and high-mobility transistor functionalities

Comprehensive Plant
Biomarker Profile for Tracing
Detection of Sulfur Mustard and Lewisite Exposure and Its Application
to Japanese Abandoned Chemical Weapon Samples
articles.abstract: Abstract Sulfur mustard (HD) and lewisite (L, mainly containing L1 and L2) from Japanese Abandoned Chemical Weapons (JACWs) in China have persisted for nearly a century, posing ongoing risks to ecological environments and public health. Plants can serve as monitoring sentinels for tracing detection of chemical exposure. However, specific plant biomarkers for HD/L remain unidentified, and their transformation in plants remains unveiled. By nontargeted metabolomics and high-resolution mass spectrometry, 30 novel plant adducts of HD/L were identified. Twelve of these adducts, along with 5 degradation products, were evaluated and assembled into a plant biomarker profile for retrospective detection of HD/L exposure. A sensitive UHPLC–TQ MS method was developed with LODs as low as 0.0200 ng/mL. The profile was detectable in 12 plant species for at least 90 days after exposure. Adduction, hydrolysis, oxidation, and trimerization of HD/L agents have been detected in plants, and transformation diagrams were portrayed. Real samples from JACW remediation sites in northeastern China were analyzed, and free biomarkers were detected at obviously higher levels in plants than in soil. Analytical results indicate that plant leaves may serve as sensitive monitoring media for the exposed agents. This work provides a reliable approach for long-term monitoring of JACW exposure and shows that possible plant accumulation and soil-to-plant transport of CWA products are valuable for further study.

articles.title:
Field Aging of Biochar
Drives SOC Accumulation by
Promoting Photosynthetic Carbon Input and Shifting Soil Microbial
Communities
articles.abstract: Abstract Biochar application is an effective strategy for enhancing the soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration. However, the extent to which biochar aging affects the SOC sequestration remains unclear. In this study, we investigated SOC dynamics, photosynthetic carbon allocation patterns, and soil microbial characteristics across a 1- to 5-year biochar aging gradient in a wheat farmland. The results revealed that the SOC content increased by 20.7% after 1 year of biochar application, primarily because of an increase in particulate organic carbon (POC), and increased by an additional 14.8% over the next 4 years, which resulted from additional increases in both POC and mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC). The total 13C assimilation increased by 19.9% and 33.0% after 1 and 5 years of biochar application, respectively. Moreover, biochar application promoted the accumulation of 13C in POC, while 5 years of biochar application also increased the assimilated 13C in MAOC. Furthermore, biochar aging altered the soil bacterial community and increased the abundance of saprotrophic fungi, which were strongly related to SOC dynamics. In summary, our results indicate that biochar aging promotes SOC sequestration by promoting photosynthetic carbon assimilation and facilitating the transformation of plant-derived carbon into SOC related to shifts in the soil microbial community.

articles.title: Combinatorial mutagenesis of N-terminal sequences reveals expanded stability determinants of the Escherichia coli N-degron pathway
Optical observation of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN photocatalyst nanostructures
articles.abstract: Abstract Understanding carrier dynamics in semiconductor nanostructures is essential for optimizing their photocatalytic performance. We present direct optical evidence of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN nanostructures used for water splitting. Two types of InGaN-based photocatalysts are studied: deepnano structures, which are a p-type InGaN micro-network, and nanowires incorporating an InGaN/GaN layered heterostructure. Here, we show that rapid lateral carrier separation in these nanostructures produces observable signatures in ultrafast spectroscopy. Using combined time-resolved photoluminescence and time-resolved differential reflectance spectroscopy, we observe photoluminescence exhibiting fast decay while differential reflection remains stable. This indicates rapid carrier separation. Studies of temperature and power-dependent photoluminescence confirm that carrier separation dominates over recombination-driven decay, and Mg doping studies reveal that stronger band bending enhances the carrier separation. The physical interpretation of the observations is supported by a numerical model including drift, diffusion, and thermal relaxation. The results provide critical insights into charge carrier dynamics in InGaN nanostructures, highlighting their potential for efficient photocatalysis.

articles.title: Wafer-scale transferable hexagonal boron nitride membranes via interfacial engineering for multilevel storage
Opposite migrations of Pacific and Atlantic tropical cyclones during the Medieval Warm Period
Wnk1 drives CD4+ T cell lineage fate determination and bone marrow homing in a mouse model of retinal autoimmune disease

Drivers of Regional
Aerosol pH Differences over Eastern
China Quantified with a Thermodynamic Framework
articles.abstract: Abstract Aerosol pH governs atmospheric multiphase chemistry, yet quantifying its regional drivers consistently across meteorologically and chemically diverse regions within a single thermodynamically accurate framework remains challenging. Here, we couple the regional chemical transport model Weather Research and Forecasting-Goddard Earth Observing System with Chemistry (WRF-GC) with the Extended Aerosol Inorganics Model (E-AIM) to compute wintertime aerosol pH over six key target regions of eastern China, decompose the drivers of regional pH differences and intramonthly variability through an ammonia gas-particle partitioning framework, and extend this framework to a scenario-response analysis. Monthly mean pH ranges from 2.54 to 4.32, more acidic in the south and more alkaline at higher latitudes. Temperature is the leading driver of the regional pH deviation in the YRD, PRD, and NEP (contributing 58%–63%), whereas in the high-emission NCP and FWP the deviation is instead dominated by NH3 (41%–58%). Negative covariance among the drivers substantially damps intramonthly pH fluctuations, consistent with multiphase buffering. The sensitivity of pH to ammonia reduction rises sharply as aerosols approach an ammonia-poor regime, such that large emission reductions of ammonia would decrease wintertime aerosol pH well beyond linear expectations, with pronounced inter-regional differences. By resolving these drivers on benchmark-level thermodynamics, these results provide a quantitative, region-specific basis for anticipating how aerosol pH responds to differentiated emission-reduction strategies.

articles.title:
Quantifying the
Vehicle Emission Reduction Required
to Offset Warming-Driven Ozone Increase in Beijing
articles.abstract: Abstract Vehicle emissions (VE) reductions are a key pathway for mitigating urban ozone pollution, but their effectiveness under the condition of warming-driven biogenic emission responses remains unclear. An ozone formation path tracing (OFPT) method coupling an observation-based model (OBM) with Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) was used to quantify the contribution of different VOCs for different emission sources to the ozone production rate (PO3). In this study, initial VOC concentrations were reconstructed by correcting for photochemical losses, and an additional constraint on isoprene was applied to improve the assessment of ozone production in Beijing. The results show that initial VOC reconstruction substantially increased PO3 and changed source attribution. Biogenic emissions became the largest single contributor to PO3, whereas VE remained the dominant controllable anthropogenic source because it supplied both VOCs and NOx. After considering the temperature response of isoprene emissions, a 10.7 ± 3.5% reduction in VE was required to offset the O3 increase caused by a 1 °C temperature rise under current conditions. Future-scenario simulations showed that the required VE reductions were lower under the Clean Air scenario (7.1 ± 0.7%) than under the Baseline scenario (11.3 ± 0.1%). These results highlight the need to integrate vehicle electrification, biogenic VOC responses, and warming effects into future ozone control strategies.

articles.title:
Depth-Dependent
eDNA Abundances across Ecosystems
Inform Deep-Sea Sampling Strategies
articles.abstract: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA) surveys are increasingly used to assess marine biodiversity and inform deep-sea environmental decision-making, including mineral resource management and fisheries oversight. Yet standard low-volume protocols inherited from coastal work may be inadequate at depth, and recent findings indicate that depth- and productivity-aware sampling, often requiring high-volume in situ filtration, is needed. Currently no quantitative framework links depth and ecosystem context to define defensible filtration volume targets. We compiled 841 eDNA samples from eight expeditions across the North Atlantic, Wider Caribbean Region, and Pacific (surface to 4000 m) to quantify how recoverable eDNA scales with depth and surface productivity, and to derive depth- and productivity-aware sampling targets. Total eDNA concentration declined with depth as a power law, with attenuation exponents (b) modulated by surface productivity: most gradual in eutrophic waters (b = 0.67), intermediate in mesotrophic (b = 0.90), and steepest in oligotrophic systems (b = 1.25). Volume-weighted models explained 66–88% of the variance. At a fixed extract-concentration target, required filtration volumes diverged ∼7-fold between oligotrophic and eutrophic systems at 200 m and ∼38-fold at 4000 m. Conventional Niskin sampling therefore undersamples deep-sea animal eDNA, particularly in mid- to low-productivity systems. Among laboratory parameters, the assay-specific extract-concentration target exerted greater leverage on required volume than extraction efficiency or elution volume. Volume-aware sampling paired with optimized recovery should be routine in deep-sea eDNA surveys.

articles.title:
Tire-Derived
Chemicals in Human Populations: A Global
Review of Exposure Pathways, Biomonitoring Evidence, Health Outcomes,
and Risk Assessment Implications
articles.abstract: Abstract Tire wear generates diverse tire-derived chemicals (TDCs), including antioxidants, accelerators, and their transformation products, yet human internal exposure remains poorly characterized. This review provides the first systematic synthesis of global biomonitoring evidence for TDCs in human populations, integrating exposure pathways, biological barrier penetration, and preliminary epidemiological findings. Biomonitoring data spanning four continents reveal widespread detection of multiple TDC classes such as p-phenylenediamines (PPDs), p-phenylenediamine quinones (PPD-Qs), benzothiazoles (BTHs), and benzotriazoles (BTRs), in urine and blood, with urinary concentrations consistently exceeding blood levels. Compound-specific patterns, including the predominance of 6PPD-Q over its parent compound 6PPD and substantial contributions from additional congeners (e.g., DPPD-Q, IPPD-Q, 1-OH-BTR), indicate that single-compound biomarkers are insufficient for capturing overall TDC exposure. TDCs have been detected in cord blood, amniotic fluid, cerebrospinal fluid, breast milk, and semen, documenting occurrence across multiple biological compartments and potential exposure during critical developmental windows. Preliminary epidemiological associations link TDC exposure to adverse birth outcomes, neurodevelopmental effects, and carcinogenic risks, though evidence remains constrained by limited sample sizes and narrow geographic representation: China-based studies dominate the literature, while regions with extensive environmental TDC monitoring (e.g., Europe, North America) largely lack corresponding human data, a mismatch that hinders exposure pathway attribution. Collectively, these findings indicate that TDCs represent a ubiquitous but underrecognized human exposure, and we outline priority considerations for risk assessment, including vulnerable population protection, congener-specific mixture effects, analytical standardization, and interim biomonitoring reference values.

articles.title:
Source
Attribution,
Driving Force Interpretation,
and Nature-Based Mitigation of Anthropogenic Water Pollution
articles.abstract: Abstract Anthropogenic pollution induced by combined sewer overflow (CSO) threatens urban aquatic ecosystems, yet the source contributions and driving mechanisms of its pollutants from surface runoff and domestic wastewater remain unclear. Here, we propose an analytical framework coupling high-resolution water quality modeling with climatic and socioeconomic (SSP-RCP) projections to characterize spatiotemporal dynamics and source contributions of CSO pollution under changing environments. Random Forest (RF) with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was employed to identify critical drivers of each source. Lorenz curves and Gini coefficient were introduced to evaluate nature-based solutions (NbS) against extreme CSOs. Application of the framework in a typical urban area demonstrated the dominant contribution of runoff pollution (78–88%) to annual loads of 2500–4200 tons, with uncertainty bounds (UB) of 2300–5800 tons. RF-SHAP analysis revealed nonlinear pollution exacerbation around transition points of approximately 8 days for dry-weather period, 0.45 for surface imperviousness, and 2000 inhabitants/km2 for population density. NbS practices mitigated 19–77% of runoff pollution and 52–76% of domestic pollution, decreasing Gini coefficients from 0.69 to 0.49 (UB: 0.40–0.82). The findings provide quantitative support for compliance with the EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive, offering a replicable reference for pollution attribution, driver identification, and mitigation assessment under changing environments.

articles.title: Dual Pathways of Fe2+ Uptake Drive Intracellular Fenton Chemistry and Ferroptosis-like Cell Death of Escherichia coli upon Exposure to Reduced Nontronite
articles.abstract: Abstract Reduced iron-containing clay (RIC) minerals display strong antibacterial activity, yet the intracellular processes underlying bacterial cell death remain poorly understood. Herein, Escherichia coli knockout strains were exposed to a model RIC mineral, reduced nontronite (rNAu-2), to dissect iron influx pathways and the resulting oxidative damage. Two complementary mechanisms of Fe2+ influx were identified: (i) active transport through FeoB proteins and (ii) passive permeation across oxidatively compromised membranes. At low rNAu-2 loading, a feoB mutant accumulated less labile Fe and survived better than the E. coli wild-type (WT), whereas at higher loading, passive permeation dominated and the genotypic differences diminished. Intracellular radical analysis revealed hydroxyl radicals (•OH) as the predominant cytotoxic species. Deleting superoxide dismutases (sodA or sodC) improved bacterial survival by limiting H2O2 availability, whereas loss of peroxidase (ahpC) or catalase (katG) activity elevated H2O2 and •OH production, and heightened cellular vulnerability. rNAu-2 exposure promoted lipid peroxidation and malondialdehyde accumulation, while increasing reliance on glutathione biosynthesis (gshA), indicative of ferroptosis-like cell death. Correspondingly, a recombination-deficient mutant (recA) was hypersensitive to rNAu-2, underscoring the role of oxidative DNA damage in bacterial cell death. These results elucidate the molecular mechanisms of RIC-mediated bacterial killing and significantly advance the current model of antibacterial clay activity.

articles.title:
Meta
Life Cycle Assessment, Techno-Economic Analysis,
and Risk Assessment of Carbon Mineralization Pathways to Inform Policy
Frameworks
articles.abstract: Abstract Carbon mineralization can reduce both point-source and legacy CO2 emissions while minimizing long-term risk, and it is essential, urgent, and disconnected. There is no holistic governing carbon mineralization policy in the US or EU, even though carbon capture is already factored into all major global climate models, with mineralization (converting CO2 into stable carbonates) representing a major subset. If mineralization is to bolster the suite of climate mitigation strategies, it is vital that academic guidance be provided to inform the currently underinformed policy direction. To address this, this study presents a meta life cycle and techno-economic analysis of carbon mineralization pathways from both academia and industry, normalizing independent techno-economic, life cycle, and risk assessment (Monte Carlo) results within the context of US and EU policy. Results demonstrate that in situ mineralization achieves the greatest life cycle GHG emission reductions at the lowest cost and is the only pathway capable of gigaton-scale emission reductions commensurate with climate goals. Enhanced rock weathering also consistently delivers net-negative GHG removal at relatively low costs, but ex situ pathways achieve lower GHG emission reductions at higher costs, where several proposed pathways are net-CO2 positive as CO2 emitted throughout the process (transportation, electricity use, and natural gas combustion) offsets CO2 sequestered. Risks of leakage, hazards, global capacity, financial impact, and reversal are also quantitatively and qualitatively compared among the mineralization pathways, demonstrating that in situ mineralization has low financial risk when bolstered by state entities, faces uncertainties in non-governmental organization objection, and, ultimately, all pathways are victims of uncharted policy.

articles.title:
GCI-TPs: Identifying
Potentially Hazardous Transformation
Products of Global Chemical Inventory Compounds
articles.abstract: Abstract Environmental contamination from an ever-increasing number of chemicals is a subject of high concern, with over one hundred thousand discrete chemicals listed in a recently compiled open global chemical inventory (GCI). As these compounds enter the environment, they often form transformation products (TPs) which may have persistent, mobile, and toxic (PMT) properties. Despite this, less than 1% of compounds have openly available TP information. Although TP prediction can fill some data gaps, the models are prone to combinatorial explosion, and predicted TPs must be prioritized. This study implemented multistep environmental biotic and novel abiotic TP prediction of the ZeroPM GCI chemicals using BioTransformer 4.0, combined with toxicity and mobility models to prioritize which TPs are potentially persistent, mobile, and toxic. The resulting GCI-TPs database contains over 13 million predicted TPs, including 5481 compounds labeled as potential dead-end compounds (compounds that are not predicted to transform further), of which 478 were predicted to be either PMT or PvM compounds. From this, 38 substructures that can act as flags for potential PMT-TP formation were identified. The dead-end PMT-TPs are available on the NORMAN Suspect List Exchange and through the GCI-TPs website (https://gcitps.lcsb.uni.lu/).

articles.title: Distinct Phyllosphere Microbiome-Linked Stress Pathways of Conventional and Biodegradable Plastics in Vallisneria natans
articles.abstract: Abstract Microplastics negatively affect submerged macrophytes, but the phyllosphere pathways associated with these responses remain poorly understood, particularly for biodegradable microplastics. Using a mesocosm experiment that distinguished fresh and withered leaf microhabitats, the stress pathways induced by conventional polystyrene (PS) and biodegradable polylactide acid (PLA) in Vallisneria natans were directly compared. Withered leaves emerged as the key microhabitat where the two polymers differed most clearly. PS was mainly associated with host-centered physiological adjustment and a modular microbial network, whereas PLA was associated with broader phyllosphere reorganization, particularly in fresh-leaf bacteria and withered-leaf algal assemblages. Direct measurements in the highest-exposure treatments detected PLA hydrolysis products (lactic acid and oligomers) and PS oxidation products, providing chemical evidence consistent with these contrasting pathways. Mantel tests and structural equation modeling further supported a divergence between a predominantly host-centered PS pathway and a broader PLA pathway involving nutrient balance and phyllosphere organization. These results indicate that conventional and biodegradable microplastics may differ not only in their direct interactions with submerged macrophytes but also in the extent to which microbiome-linked indirect pathways are involved.

articles.title:
An
Innovative Ion Chromatography Method for Determination
of Hydroxymethanesulfonate (HMS) in Ambient Air
articles.abstract: Abstract Hydroxymethanesulfonate (HMS) is a substantial contributor to atmospheric particulate sulfur, yet its accurate quantification remains challenging due to chemical instability, poor chromatographic separation from sulfate, and the lack of a robust routine filter method. Here, we developed a hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-based differential ion chromatography method that overcomes these limitations. Under optimized conditions (n(H2O2):n(HMS) ≥ 4:1, 60 °C, 30 min), HMS conversion to sulfate reaches 97.5 ± 0.3%, enabling indirect quantification via the stable sulfate signal. Recovery on spiked filters was 99.6 ± 1.4% across 0.025–10 mg L–1, with a method detection limit of 0.018 mg L–1. Application to ∼180 PM2.5 samples from a rural North China Plain site shows HMS is not confined to winter haze: autumn concentrations (mean 0.59 ± 0.70 μg m–3, maximum 3.75 μg m–3) were comparable to or higher than winter values, associated with high relative humidity and elevated formaldehyde. Archived filters lost ∼25% of HMS within one month, suggesting historical data may be biased low. The relative contribution of HMS to particulate sulfur increases as total sulfur loading decreases, implying SO2 emission reductions alone may not diminish HMS chemistry. This method provides a robust framework for accurate HMS measurement and improved sulfur budget closure.

articles.title:
Shrinking Non-CO2 Emission Inequality in
China’s Municipal Wastewater Treatment
articles.abstract: Abstract Integrating emission equity into climate mitigation is essential for sustainable development but remains poorly understood in the wastewater-treatment sector. Here, we develop a long-term, high-resolution emission inventory covering 8703 municipal wastewater treatment plants across China from 2001 to 2020 to assess methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) emission trends and their spatial inequality. National emissions increased substantially, although growth rates slowed after 2010 for CH4 and 2015 for N2O. Discrepancies with IPCC-derived estimates highlight the limitations of population-based approaches in capturing emission trends. Economic development dominated emission growth, with wastewater treatment intensity (wastewater treated per unit of GDP) contributing positively, even under scenarios that account for potential changes in emission factors associated with technological and management improvements. Significant emission inequality persisted, with economically developed cities (9% of the population) contributing 16% and 15% of CH4 and N2O emissions in 2020, whereas the least developed group (45% of the population) accounted for 28% and 32%, respectively. Nonetheless, this disparity narrowed over time with Gini coefficients falling from 0.54 to 0.26 for CH4 and from 0.51 to 0.22 for N2O. These findings support geographically differentiated mitigation strategies that prioritize high-emitting areas to promote effective and equitable climate mitigation.

articles.title:
Enhancing Sewer
Sediment Permeability via Micro-nano
Bubble–Mediated Structural Remodeling and EPS Reduction
articles.abstract: Abstract Sewer sediments contain dense biofilms enriched with extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), which severely impede chemical infiltration and hinder sediment control. This study uses micro-nano bubbles (MNBs) for the first time to remodel the three-dimensional structure of sewer sediments and reduce their EPS content, thereby enhancing their permeability. Three-dimensional structural analysis revealed that sewer sediments consist of cluster (0.78 mm) and bridged (0.12 mm) biofilms, forming a dense gel network with low porosity. When 20% MNBs were introduced, the complete tracer penetration time decreased from 36 to 8 h, representing a 3.5-times faster migration speed than the baseline group. X-ray computed tomography revealed that MNBs disrupted the sediment matrix: tortuosity decreased from 1.754 to 1.352, the pore volume fraction increased from 0.083 to 0.105, and the number of cluster biofilms decreased from 280 to 178. EPS analysis indicated substantial depth-dependent reductions in protein (5.6 to 1.4 mg/g VSS) and polysaccharide (3.8 to 1.9 mg/g VSS) contents. Finally, the oxidation–reduction potential increased from −280 to −88 mV, shifting the dominant microbial community from anaerobic to aerobic. The underlying mechanism involved the synergistic effects of structural remodeling and EPS reduction, providing theoretical support for applying MNB technology to urban sewage pipe maintenance.

articles.title:
Proton-Coupled
Oxidation
Mechanisms in the Ferrate
System: Unraveling the pH Dependence of Fe(VI), Fe(V), and Fe(IV)
for Contaminant Abatement
articles.abstract: Abstract Like conventional water treatment oxidants, ferrate exhibits highly pH-dependent reaction kinetics, classically attributed to its acid–base speciation. However, while this dissociation equilibrium accurately describes the kinetics of ferrate decay, it cannot account for the anomalous pH-dependent kinetics observed during contaminant oxidation. By combining acid–base model with the pyrophosphate sequestering method, we reveal that highly reactive Fe(V) and Fe(IV) intermediates drive this deviation. To trace these species, aniline, theophylline, and sulfamethoxazole were employed as model contaminants for oxidation processes dominated by Fe(VI), Fe(V), and Fe(IV), respectively. By quantifying their specific contributions, we found that decreasing pH enhances the reactivity of the intermediates and amplifies their oxidation contributions by 13–63%. Consequently, the systems dominated by Fe(V) or Fe(IV) exhibit apparent rate constants surging far beyond the predictive capacity of the Fe(VI) speciation. Solvent kinetic isotope effects and proton inventory analyses elucidated distinct proton-assisted pathways: Fe(VI) undergoes a rapid protonation pre-equilibrium before rate-limiting electron transfer, Fe(V) reacts via a concerted proton–electron transfer pathway, and Fe(IV) proceeds through an inner-sphere electron transfer pathway associated with coordinated water release. Exploiting these insights, we demonstrate a proton-activation strategy where rapid proton exchange significantly enhances both reaction kinetics and oxidant utilization efficiency in ferrate-based water treatment.

articles.title: Physiological Adaptation of Comammox Nitrospira to Acidic pH Suppresses N2O Production
articles.abstract: Abstract Nitrous oxide (N2O), a potent greenhouse gas, is a major byproduct of microbial nitrification, yet how environmental pH governs N2O production by complete ammonia oxidizers (comammox) remains poorly understood. We conducted controlled culture experiments with comammox Nitrospira inopinata at pH 6.5, 7.5, and 8.5. Under mild acidification (pH 6.5), nitrification activity was largely maintained, but cellular growth declined sharply, and both N2O yield and extracellular hydroxylamine (NH2OH) accumulation fell substantially relative to neutral conditions. Strikingly, this reduced growth was accompanied by pronounced transcriptional upregulation of core nitrification, stress response, and pH homeostasis genes, whereas carbon fixation genes remained largely unchanged. This decoupling of growth from gene expression indicates that acid-stressed cells reallocate energy away from biosynthesis toward cellular maintenance and proton extrusion, tightening intracellular handling of NH2OH and limiting its extracellular release. Isotopomer analysis (site preference ∼28–36‰) confirmed that NH2OH-driven chemistry remained the dominant N2O source across all pH conditions, and complementary abiotic assays indicated that chemical N2O formation was likely influenced by the diminished NH2OH pool. These results establish that comammox suppresses, rather than enhances, N2O production under mild acidification, opposite to the response reported for canonical ammonia-oxidizing microbes. This distinctive trait carries important implications for predicting nitrification-derived N2O fluxes and refining greenhouse-gas budgets in acidifying ecosystems.

articles.title:
Per-
and Polyfluoroalkyl
Substances (PFAS) in Textiles:
Attributing the Fluorine Inventory via Polymer-Specific Analysis
articles.abstract: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used in functional textiles for water- and stain resistance, yet their polymer compositions, quantities, and potential environmental release remain poorly resolved by conventional analyses. Here, we analyzed 22 commercial textiles using an integrated approach combining total fluorine (TF) by combustion ion chromatography, targeted PFAS analysis, the total oxidizable precursor (TOP) assay, and pyrolysis–gas chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (Py-GC-HRMS); the latter enabled polymer-specific identification and semiquantitative estimation of fluoropolymer and side-chain fluorinated polymer (SCFP) contributions. Fifteen textiles contained low-to-moderate TF concentrations (0.03–2.57 mg F g–1) and were predominantly associated with SCFPs containing 6:2 and/or 8:2 fluorotelomer moieties, whereas three high-fluorine textiles (143–158 mg F g–1) contained polytetrafluoroethylene together with SCFP-based treatments. Targeted PFAS accounted for ≤0.021% of TF, while TOP-derived PFAS also represented only a small additional fraction, indicating that conventional extractable and oxidizable PFAS measurements captured little of the total fluorine inventory. Simulated laundering, UV exposure, and wet abrasion caused limited TF loss in most textiles but substantial losses in some SCFP-treated materials, indicating treatment-dependent potential for PFAS-associated fluorine release during use and aging. This approach improves polymer-specific characterization of PFAS in textiles and helps assess their potential environmental emissions.

articles.title:
Decoding and Harnessing
Microbial Resilience for Anaerobic
Digestion: Mechanisms, Strategies, and Sustainability under Environmental
Stress
articles.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic digestion (AD) is central to the circular bioeconomy, yet its application is limited by the vulnerability of microbial consortia to diverse stressors from endogenous metabolic inhibitors to exogenous contaminants. This Review synthesizes current evidence on microbial resilience mechanisms in AD, distinguishing resistance from perturbation to functional recovery through a sensing-activation-adaptation cascade. The thermodynamic basis of stability is examined through discoveries in direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) and metabolic bifurcation, revealing how syntrophic networks overcome thermodynamic barriers under stress. Multiscale resilience mechanisms are considered from molecular sensors and signal transduction pathways to community-level reorganization associated with functional redundancy and niche differentiation. Bridging microbial ecology with process engineering, resilience-enhancing strategies are evaluated, including quorum sensing manipulation, conductive material amendment, and bioaugmentation with immobilized consortia, strengthening syntrophic networks under internal and external perturbations. A shift from reactive monitoring to proactive management is discussed, using interpretable deep learning models and genome-informed digital twins to predict failures. Critical knowledge gaps include single-cell phenotypic heterogeneity and the synthetic consortium design. Resilient AD systems require a framework integrating techno-economic viability with life cycle assessment, ensuring that they are biologically robust, environmentally sustainable, and economically competitive under variable operating conditions.

articles.title:
Underappreciated
Role of Free Troposphere–Boundary
Layer Exchange in Ozone Pollution over the North China Plain
articles.abstract: Abstract Ozone pollution control is mainly based on the ozone chemistry sensitivity to precursor emissions. However, despite stringent reductions in precursor emissions, severe summer ozone pollution persistently engulfs the North China Plain (NCP), urgently calling for effective ozone controls. Here, we show that there is strong interfacial ozone exchange between free troposphere (FT) and atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), which renders FT ozone a potential source of surface ozone, but has not been well accounted for in previous ozone controls. We quantify FT-ABL interfacial ozone exchange using an online diagnostic scheme implemented in a coupled meteorology-chemistry model and reveal a significant yet spatially heterogeneous correlation between observed surface ozone and interfacial exchange over the NCP. In high-correlation area, strong downward transport from FT to ABL exceeds chemical production, contributing 52% of afternoon ozone sources under polluted conditions. In low-correlation area, ozone pollution is dominated by chemical production. Derived from these spatially differentiated pollution causes, we propose an expanded ozone pollution formation regime to divide the NCP into exchange-dominated, chemistry-dominated, and mixed conditions. This new regime can better explain observed and modeled spatial differences of ozone trends in response to precursor reductions in 2019–2025. Our results highlight the importance of incorporating FT-ABL interfacial exchange into ozone pollution control frameworks beyond conventional chemistry-based regime.

articles.title: Mechanochemistry-Induced Hydrated Salt Activation for Green Recovery of Palladium and Platinum via O 2 -Mediated Oxidation
articles.abstract: Abstract Palladium (Pd) and platinum (Pt) are essential precious metals in modern catalytic applications, while their sustainable recovery remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a room-temperature, AlCl3·6H2O-assisted mechanochemical strategy for efficient recovery of Pd and Pt from industrial spent catalysts and automotive three-way catalysts without the addition of external oxidants. Mechanistic investigations reveal that mechanochemical treatment promotes catalyst fragmentation and the activation of hydrated salt, creating an ion-rich, liquid-like interfacial environment that facilitates O2-mediated oxidation of metallic Pd and Pt and stabilizes the oxidized metal species through chloride coordination. High-purity Pd and Pt products were successfully recovered through water extraction and N2H4·H2O reduction, while the recyclable AlCl3·6H2O medium enabled a closed-loop process with reduced reagent consumption. A preliminary lab-scale cost assessment indicated treatment costs comparable to those of conventional aqua regia treatment, highlighting the potential of hydrated salt-assisted mechanochemistry as a mild, recyclable, and economically promising approach for sustainable Pd and Pt recovery.
